 Reminder: Washington overtime salary thresholds increase January 1
 November 12, 2026 
 Washington employers should review employee compensation ahead of the new year as the state’s minimum salary requirements for certain overtime-exempt employees are scheduled to increase January 1, 2027.   
 The overtime exemption salary threshold is tied to Washington’s minimum wage and calculated using a multiplier of a 40-hour workweek. To qualify for an overtime exemption, employees generally must meet both the applicable salary threshold and job duties requirements.   
 The projected 2027 salary thresholds are:   
 Small employers (1–50 employees): $1,583.10 per week, or $82,321.20 annually.   
 Large employers (51 or more employees): $1,759 per week, or $91,468 annually.   
 Retailers should review salaries for currently exempt employees to determine whether compensation adjustments or changes to employee classifications may be necessary. Employers should also factor the increases into 2027 staffing and budget plans.
